topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the lecture series context, and the core learning outcomes concerning cancer causation and environmental carcinogens.

topics.label: Conceptual Frameworks and Epidemiological Evidence for Cancer Causation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational concepts of how cancer arises through an interplay of intrinsic biological errors, genetic predispositions, and environmental exposures supported by global epidemiological data.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Action of Cancer Initiators and Promoters
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular and cellular mechanisms by which various environmental agents induce DNA damage, drive tumour promotion, or exhibit tissue-specific carcinogenic effects.

topics.label: Methodologies for Determining Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to demonstrate and measure the carcinogenic potential of environmental exposures.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with summary remarks on the challenges of carcinogen evaluation and the everyday balancing of cancer risks and benefits.
